description: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of named entity types identified within a biomedical text corpus. The chart contains 16 slices, each representing a different entity type. The largest slice, labeled “Protein,” is blue and occupies approximately 37% of the chart. “DNA” is represented by a green slice at approximately 8%. “Chemical Family” is shown in orange and accounts for roughly 7%, while “Disease” is pink and represents about 4%. The remaining slices, representing entity types such as “Cell Type,” “Drug,” “Frequency,” “Cell Line,” “Strength,” “Form,” “Gene Or Gene Product,” “Disease Or Phenotypic Feature,” “Specific Disease,” “Reason,” “Route,” “Chemical Entity,” “Sequence Variant,” “Mutation,” “Organism taxon,” and “Composite Mention,” are all relatively small, ranging from approximately 1% to 3%. A legend is present, labeling each slice with its corresponding entity type. Percentage labels are not displayed directly within the slices, but are provided in the legend. The slices appear to be ordered visually in descending order based on their proportional size.
